body.statement:
Under \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), the globally completed active tangent arrangement has a full-dimensional strict chamber unless there are no active cuts, in which case its unique component is \(\mathbb R^d\).  The canonical search returns \(P_{v_*,b_*}^0\), a rational point \(u_*\), and exact rational linear-programming certificates such that \(\rho_0>0\).  With \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\),
\[
 \{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\},\qquad
 \inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\ge r_0.
\]
Thus \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\) for \(\mathfrak G_0\) without a causal margin assumption.
body.justification: A strict chamber and its rational row-distance receipt now rest on causally legal tangent geometry.
body.gap: The finite hyperplane and Mahalanobis calculations close after the corrected cover is applied.
body.consumer: The receipt verifies the separated-domain premise before CertGluePFL is invoked.
body.proof_tex:
If the active list is nonempty, its members are nonzero rational normals.  A finite union of their hyperplanes cannot contain an open ball, so its complement has a nonempty full-dimensional chamber.  Rational points are dense in that open chamber.  By the global-cover proposition and the convention that fixed ties with identical completed regions have one semantic representative, this strict sign chamber lies in a unique semantic component \(P_{v,b}^0\).  At a rational strict point all of its nonredundant defining inequalities have positive slack.  Scaling within the homogeneous chamber and using \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\) shows that the positive-margin linear program used to define \(i_*\) has optimum \(1\) for at least one component.  Therefore the canonical finite search finds a component with positive margin and returns a rational basic solution \(u_*\) in its strict chamber.  If the active list is empty, the prescribed choice \(u_*=0\) lies in the unique component \(\mathbb R^d\).  Thus in both cases
\[
 \{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\}.
\tag{1}
\]

Consider a retained rival component
\[
 P_{v,b}^0=\{g:A_{v,b}^0g\leq b_{v,b}^0\},\qquad v\ne v_*.
\tag{2}
\]
It cannot contain \(u_*\), by (1).  Since (2) is exactly the intersection of its displayed closed halfspaces, at least one displayed row \(i\) has the rational gap
\[
 \gamma_{v,b,i}=(A_{v,b}^0u_*-b_{v,b}^0)_i>0.
\tag{3}
\]
That row is nonzero.  The base law has strictly positive cells and \(B\) has full column rank, so
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0
 \quad(x\ne0),
\tag{4}
\]
and hence \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  Therefore the row norm \(\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}\) is positive.  For every \(g\in P_{v,b}^0\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \gamma_{v,b,i}
 &\leq (A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}(u_*-g)\\
 &\leq \|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}
       \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
If the rational bisection receipt gives \(s_{v,b,i}\geq\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}>0\), (5) yields
\[
 \inf_{g\in P_{v,b}^0}\|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \geq\frac{\gamma_{v,b,i}}{s_{v,b,i}}=\rho_{v,b}>0.
\tag{6}
\]
There are finitely many rival components, so the minimum defining \(\rho_0\) is positive; if there is no rival, it equals the included value \(1\).  Since \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\), taking the minimum of (6) over the components of every rival semantic union gives
\[
 \inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\geq\rho_0\geq r_0.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (1) and (7) put \(u_*\) in \(H_{r_0}\).  All chamber, row-gap, norm-enclosure, and minimum operations are finite rational computations, which proves the asserted exact certificates and the nonempty separated domain without a causal margin premise.
